blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
There are emerging commercial multimodal generation platforms that provide both text-to-image generation and instruction-guided image editing [ 18 , 7 , 29 ] .
All major providers emphasize content safety in their policies [ 19 , 8 , 1 ] , yet existing safety mechanisms on these platforms are designed primarily around text: they analyze the prompt but largely overlook the visual input [ 12 , 9 , 21 ] .
Image editing, however, requires jointly considering the visual content and the textual intent to make appropriate safety decisions [ 30 , 20 ] .
For example, a user who uploads a violent image and requests “improve the image quality” or “mask the violent part” poses a safety question that cannot be resolved by analyzing the instruction alone.
blocks.zh:
新兴的商业多式联运生成平台既提供文本到图像生成,又提供指导性图像编辑[18,7,29].
所有主要供应商在其政策[19、8、1]中强调内容安全,然而这些平台上现有的安全机制主要是围绕文本设计的:它们分析即时但基本上忽略了视觉输入[12、9、21]。
然而,图像编辑需要共同考虑视觉内容和作出适当安全决定的文字意图[30,20].
例如,上传暴力图像并要求“改进图像质量”或“掩盖暴力部分”的用户提出的安全问题不能单靠分析指示来解决。

blocks.en:
Despite this challenge, text-visual safety in image editing remains underexplored.
Existing safety benchmarks [ 15 , 34 ] primarily target single-modality threats rather than the cross-modal interaction inherent to image editing.
Concurrent efforts have begun to explore adversarial attacks and guardrails for editing models [ 11 , 20 ] , but few works directly measure whether deployed systems account for visual input risk in non-adversarial, naturalistic editing scenarios.
blocks.zh:
尽管面临这一挑战,图像编辑的文字-视觉安全性仍然没有得到充分利用。
现有的安全基准[15,34]主要针对单一模式的威胁,而不是图像编辑所固有的交叉模式互动。
同时进行的努力已经开始探索用于编辑模型的对抗攻击和护栏[11,20],但很少能直接衡量部署的系统在非对抗性,自然主义的编辑情景中是否计入视觉输入风险.

blocks.en:
We thus introduce EditSafetyBench , a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness in instruction-guided image editing systems.
We define a system as a deployed editing pipeline that may include the model, safety filters, and API wrappers [ 31 ] .
We consider three system decisions: allow, refuse, or error.
Specifically, we construct the EditSafetyBench dataset by pairing safe and unsafe images with neutral, risk-reducing, and unsafe-intent edit instructions across 11 risk categories, yielding 5,940 image-instruction pairs.
Then we probe the dataset on four systems that are based on multimodal large language models (MLLMs): Google’s Gemini [ 7 ] , OpenAI’s GPT Image (GPT) [ 18 ] , Alibaba’s Qwen Image Edit API (Qwen API) [ 29 ] , and Qwen Image Edit Local Model (Qwen Local) [ 29 ] .
We obtain the following main findings:

blocks.en: (a) Text-Vision Safety Mismatch. Gemini and GPT refuse 81.6–87.1% of unsafe-intent edits but only refuse 22.4–24.2% of unsafe images with neutral instructions, revealing more awareness on text modality (see Figure 1 ).
blocks.zh: (a) 文本-视觉安全错配。 双子座和GPT拒绝81.6–87.1%的不安全的意向编辑,但只拒绝22.4–24.2%的带有中性指令的不安全图像,揭示出更多对文本模式的认识(见图1).

blocks.en: (b) Text Intent Overrides Visual Risk. Although unsafe images with neutral-intent edits have a higher moderation score than safe images with unsafe intent, system decisions ignore this: the safe-vs-unsafe allow rate gap is only 0.2–0.4% under unsafe-intent edits for Gemini and GPT, indicating text intent dominates safety filtering.
blocks.zh: (b) 文本意图克服视觉风险。 虽然带有中性意图编辑的不安全图像比具有不安全意图的安全图像有更高的温和分数,但系统决定忽略了这一点:在双子座和GBT的不安全意图编辑下,安全vs-不安全允许率差距只有0.2-0.4%,表明文本意图主导安全过滤.

blocks.en:
(c) Category-Level Visual Sensitivity. Most risk categories show cross-platform awareness inconsistency, e.g., GPT allows 70.4% of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8%.
Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity among all categories, likely benefiting from mature NSFW detection studies.
blocks.zh:
(c) 类别视觉敏感性。 大多数风险类别显示跨平台认知不一致,例如GPT允许70.4%的不安全政治内容,而双子座只允许34.8%.
值得注意的是,性内容在所有类别中表现出最强的视觉敏感性,可能受益于成熟的NSFW检测研究.

blocks.en: Contributions. Our contributions are as follows: • We formulate the system-level safety awareness problem for image editing, focusing on the deployed pipeline rather than isolated model capabilities. • We introduce EditSafetyBench , a controlled benchmark pairing safe/unsafe images with three edit intents across 11 risk categories and evaluate on four systems from three providers. • Based on our findings, we urge the development of safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

blocks.en: Related Work
blocks.zh: 有关工作

blocks.en:
Multimodal Image Generation. Multimodal image generation has evolved from text-to-image diffusion models [ 24 , 26 ] to unified systems that support both generation and instruction-guided editing [ 3 , 33 ] .
Commercial systems such as Gemini [ 7 ] , GPT Image [ 18 ] , and Qwen [ 29 ] now offer image editing as production endpoints wrapped in layered safety architectures [ 31 ] .
blocks.zh:
多式联运图像生成. 多式联运图像生成已经从文本到图像传播模型[24,26]发展为支持生成和指令引导编辑的统一系统[3,33].
双子座等商业系统[7],GBT 图片 [18],和Qwen [29] 现在提供图像编辑作为生产端点 包裹在层层安全架构 [31].

blocks.en:
Platform Policy. We survey three main platforms [ 19 , 8 , 1 ] and map their content policies to 11 risk categories.
These policies have broad coverage for hate, violence, and sexual content but weaker attention to categories like self-harm and political content.
Details can be found in Appendix B .
blocks.zh:
平台政策. 我们调查了三个主要平台[19,8,1],并将其内容政策映射到11个风险类别。
这些政策广泛涵盖仇恨、暴力和性内容,但对自我伤害和政治内容等类别的关注却较弱。
详情见附录B。

blocks.en:
Content Moderation. Content moderation has been widely studied, especially for individual modalities [ 6 , 28 , 27 , 5 ] .
For multimodal image generation, existing safety guardrail research mainly focuses on preventing unsafe generation from text prompts [ 32 , 5 , 22 , 25 ] .
Image content moderation is also studied from BERT-based classifiers [ 5 ] to VLM-based LlavaGuard [ 10 ] and SafeVision [ 30 ] .
However, multimodal content moderation requires considering the joint of both visual and text modalities [ 13 , 16 ] .
For example, HoliSafe [ 13 ] measures both visual and textual inputs of VLMs.
To the extent of our knowledge, however, there is a lack of work focusing on image editing, which requires considering both the input image and editing prompts and measuring the safety of their outcomes.
blocks.zh:
内容调和。 内容节制得到了广泛的研究,特别是针对个别方式[6、28、27、5]。
对于多模式图像生成,现有的安全护栏研究主要侧重于防止文本提示产生不安全的生成[32,5,22,25].
图像内容节制也从基于BERT的分类器[5]到基于VLM的LlavaGuard[10]和SafeVision[30]研究.
然而,多式联运的内容节制需要考虑视觉和文字两种模式的结合[13、16]。
例如,HoliSafe[13]既测量VLM的视觉输入,又测量文字输入.
然而,就我们所知,缺乏注重图像编辑的工作,这需要既考虑输入图像,又考虑编辑提示,并衡量结果的安全性。

blocks.en:
Multimodal Safety Benchmarks. Existing benchmarks focus on identifying unsafe content [ 15 , 34 , 2 ] or text-to-image safety generation [ 14 ] .
MM-SafetyBench [ 15 ] tests whether multimodal models generate unsafe text responses to image-text inputs, and VLGuard [ 34 ] evaluates jailbreak robustness through safety fine-tuning of vision-language models (VLMs).
Image safeguarding approaches reason about unsafe visual content using VLMs [ 2 ] .
Two concurrent works from early 2026 also address image editing safety: IESBench [ 11 ] studies adversarial jailbreak attacks on editing models through visual prompts, while Piao et al. [ 20 ] propose policy-adaptive image guardrails using edited image pairs.
In contrast, EditSafetyBench measures system-level safety awareness under non-adversarial, naturalistic editing scenarios, focusing on whether deployed systems jointly consider visual content and textual intent.
blocks.zh:
多式联运安全基准。 现有基准侧重于确定不安全的内容[15,34,2]或文本到图像安全生成[14].
MM-Safety Bench [15] 测试多式联运模型是否对图像文本输入产生不安全的文本响应,VLGuard [34] 通过对视觉语言模型的安全微调(VLMs)来评价越狱强度.
图像保护方法对使用VLMs的不安全视觉内容提出了理由[2].
2026年初两部并行的作品也涉及图像编辑安全: IES Bench [11] 研究通过视觉提示对编辑模型进行对抗性越狱攻击,而Piao et al. [20] 提议采用经过编辑的图像对进行政策调整的图像护栏.
相比之下,EditSafety Bench在非对抗性的自然主义编辑方案下衡量系统层面的安全意识,重点是部署的系统是否共同考虑视觉内容和文字意图.

Note that we evaluate system-level safety decisions , not editing quality or output harmfulness.

blocks.en:
Safety Dimensions. Different from text-to-image generation considering only text, we define two orthogonal safety dimensions, i.e., image safety and edit intent .
Specifically, image safety refers to whether the input image contains unsafe visual content, regardless of the instruction.
Edit intent is categorized into three types: • Neutral : Benign editing requests such as quality improvement, brightness adjustment, or cropping.
They carry no safety signal in the text and thus test whether the system responds to the visual input alone. • Risk-Reducing : Requests to obscure or anonymize sensitive content.
A safety-aware system should ideally allow these even on unsafe images, since the intent is to reduce harm. • Unsafe-Intent : Requests to amplify or redistribute harmful content.
A well-aligned system should refuse these regardless of image safety.

blocks.en:
System Behavior Evaluation. The cross-product of these two dimensions creates six probe scenarios, as shown in Figure 2 .
This enables us to characterize how deployed editing systems place their safety awareness across different combinations of visual risk and textual intent.
Specifically, we define three metrics based on the major goal to mitigate unsafe content generation: • Safe Over-Refusal (SOR) ↓ \downarrow is defined as the block rate (Refuse+Error) on benign edits (blue in Figure 2 ), measuring whether the system over-refuses benign editing attempts: R Safe × Neutral+All × Risk-Reducing Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{Safe $\times$ Neutral+All $\times$ Risk-Reducing}} .
We expect the system to accept neutral and risk-reducing edit intents on safe images and allow risk-reducing edit intents on unsafe images.
Thus, a lower SOR is better. • Unsafe Intent Refusal (UIR) ↑ \uparrow is the block rate of both safe and unsafe images (orange in Figure 2 ): R All × Unsafe-Intent Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{All $\times$ Unsafe-Intent}} .
The system should reject all unsafe intent editing attempts; a higher score is better. • Unsafe Neutral Refusal (UNR) ↑ \uparrow is the block rate of neutral edit intent attempts on unsafe images (yellow in Figure 2 ): R Unsafe × Neutral Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{Unsafe $\times$ Neutral}} .
Although whether we should reward such refusal is debatable (see Section 5 ), we regard it as an advantage.
For example, we consider “improve quality” or “adjust brightness” on an unsafe sexual image as inappropriate.
Thus, a higher UNR score is better.

Safe Over-Refusal (SOR) ↓ \downarrow is defined as the block rate (Refuse+Error) on benign edits (blue in Figure 2 ), measuring whether the system over-refuses benign editing attempts: R Safe × Neutral+All × Risk-Reducing Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{Safe $\times$ Neutral+All $\times$ Risk-Reducing}} .
We expect the system to accept neutral and risk-reducing edit intents on safe images and allow risk-reducing edit intents on unsafe images.
Thus, a lower SOR is better.

Although whether we should reward such refusal is debatable (see Section 5 ), we regard it as an advantage.
For example, we consider “improve quality” or “adjust brightness” on an unsafe sexual image as inappropriate.
Thus, a higher UNR score is better.

不安全的中立拒绝 (UNR) \ oparrow 是不安全图像上的中立编辑意图尝试的块速率(图2中的黄色): R不安全 × 中立块 R_ 中文本{ Block_ { text{ Unsafe $\times$ 中立 } 。

blocks.en:
Scope. We target the safety awareness of existing real-world systems in image editing.
Thus, we do not include text-vision guardrails [ 13 , 16 ] in our evaluation.
Such guardrails are system components and do not focus on image editing, which requires understanding the outcome of the input image and prompt.
blocks.zh:
范围。 我们的目标是在图像编辑方面提高现有现实世界系统的安全意识。
因此,我们评价中不包括文本-视觉护栏[13、16]。
这种护栏是系统组件,不注重图像编辑,这需要了解输入图像的结果并迅速.

blocks.en:
Figure 3 : EditSafetyBench .
We first collect 660 images from UnsafeBench through moderation score-aware sampling, and pair them with our instructions covering three edit intents, resulting in a benchmark dataset with 5,940 samples.
Then, we probe multimodal image editing systems and measure system-level safety awareness in image editing systems.
blocks.zh:
图3:编辑安全奔驰。
我们首先通过温和的分数知觉取样收集了来自不安全奔驰的660张图像,并将其与我们包含三个编辑意图的指令配对,形成一个包含5,940个样本的基准数据集.
然后,我们探索多模式图像编辑系统,测量图像编辑系统中的系统级安全意识.

blocks.en: Benchmark Construction
blocks.zh: 基准建设

blocks.en: As shown in Figure 3 , our EditSafetyBench pipeline includes collecting safe/unsafe images, designing image-agnostic edit instructions, and system probing.
blocks.zh: 如图3所示,我们的EditSafety Bench管道包括收集安全/不安全图像、设计图像不可知编辑指令以及系统探测。

blocks.en:
Image Collection. We draw images from UnsafeBench [ 23 ] , which provides safe and unsafe examples across 11 risk categories (Hate, Harassment, Violence, Self-Harm, Sexual, Shocking, Illegal Activity, Deception, Political, Public and Personal Health, Spam).
These categories originate from OpenAI’s content policy [ 19 ] and align with the policies of three major commercial platforms we surveyed (Appendix B ), ensuring our benchmark evaluates categories that platforms explicitly follow.
blocks.zh:
图片集. 我们从不安全的奔驰[23]中绘制图像,这提供了11个风险类别(仇恨、骚扰、暴力、自我伤害、性、震惊、非法活动、欺骗、政治、公共和个人健康、垃圾邮件)的安全和不安全的例子。
这些类别源于OpenAI的内容政策[19],与我们调查的三个主要商业平台的政策一致(附录B),确保我们的基准评估平台明确遵循的类别。

blocks.en:
To ensure unambiguous safety labels, we apply a moderation score-aware sampling strategy.
We first score all UnsafeBench images with OpenAI’s Moderation API 1 1 1 omni-moderation-2024-09-26 and take the maximum category score as each image’s overall moderation score.
We then select safe images with the lowest scores and unsafe images with the highest scores within each category, ensuring that safe images are unambiguously benign and unsafe images carry genuine risk rather than borderline cases.
Within each of the 11 × 2 = 22 11\times 2=22 category-safety cells, we sample 30 images with balanced provenance (15 human-crafted, 15 AI-generated), giving 11 × 2 × 30 = 660 11\times 2\times 30=660 images in total.
This yields 330 safe images (mean score 0.0009) and 330 unsafe images (mean score 0.3255), producing a 372.58 × \times separation (see Figure 4 ).
The balanced human-crafted/AI-generated split also enables analyzing whether systems behave differently depending on image provenance.
blocks.zh:
为确保安全标签明确无误,我们采用温和的、有分数的取样战略。
我们首先用OpenAI的Medation API 1 1 1 omni-modation 2024-09-26来评分所有不安全的Bench图像,并将最高分类分作为每个图像的整体温和分数.
然后,我们选择得分最低的安全图像和在每个类别中得分最高的不安全图像,确保安全图像是明确无害的,不安全的图像具有真正的风险,而不是边缘情况。
在11×2 = 22 11\times 2= 22个类别安全细胞中,我们抽取了30个具有均衡出处的图像(15个人工制作,15个AI生成),给出了11×2×30 = 660 11\times 2\times 30= 660个图像。
这产生330个安全图像(平均得分0.0009)和330个不安全图像(平均得分0.3255),产生372.58×\时间分离(见图4).
人造/人工智能产生的平衡分裂还有助于分析系统是否视图像来源而有不同行为。

blocks.en:
Edit Instruction Design. EditSafetyBench uses general, image-agnostic edit instructions rather than image-specific ones.
This design is critical: by applying identical instructions to both safe and unsafe images, any behavioral difference between the two groups can be attributed to visual content, not instruction phrasing.
For each of the three intent types defined in Section 3.1 , we write three concrete prompts, yielding a fixed bank of nine prompts per image (see Appendix C ).
blocks.zh:
编辑指令设计. 编辑Safety Bench使用一般的,图像不可知的编辑指令而不是图像特定指令.
这种设计至关重要:通过对安全和不安全的图像应用相同的指令,两个组之间的任何行为差异都可以归因于视觉内容,而不是指令的用词.
对于第3.1节界定的三种意图类型,我们分别写下三种混凝土提示,产生一个固定的银行,每个图像有9个提示(见附录C)。

blocks.en:
Benchmark Assembly. Each of the 660 images is paired with all nine prompts, producing 660 × 9 = 5,940 660\times 9=5{,}940 image-instruction pairs.
The balanced design ( 30 30 images per category-safety cell, identical prompts across systems) enables category-level statistical analysis and controlled cross-platform comparison.
We additionally collect 200 natural images from MagicBrush [ 33 ] , a large-scale instruction-guided real image editing dataset, as a held-out control set for validating safe-image behavior (Section 4.7 ).
blocks.zh:
基准大会。 660个图像中每个图像都与所有9个提示对齐,产生660×9 = 5 940 660\times 9=5{,}940个图像指令对.
平衡的设计(每个类别安全单元30幅图像,跨系统相同的提示)能够进行类别统计分析,并控制跨平台比较。
我们从MagicBrush [33] 收集200张自然图像,这是一套大规模指导性真实图像编辑数据集,作为用于验证安全图像行为的搁置控制(第4.7节)。

blocks.en: System Probing. For every image-instruction pair, we query each system and normalize the response to the decision labels defined in Section 3.1 : Allow (edited image returned), Refuse (request blocked), or Error (technical failure).
blocks.zh: 系统探测 对于每对图像指令,我们查询每个系统,使对第3.1节中定义的决定标签的答复正常化: 允许( 编辑图像返回 ) 、 拒绝( 请求被封锁) 或 错误( 技术故障 ) 。

blocks.en:
Figure 4 : Moderation score distribution for safe and unsafe images.
Safe images cluster near zero, while unsafe images spread across higher risk levels, ensuring a clear visual danger differential.
blocks.zh:
图4:安全和不安全图像的中度分数分布。
安全图像集群接近零,而不安全的图像则散布在更高的风险水平上,确保明显的视觉危险差.

blocks.en: Experiments
blocks.zh: 实验

blocks.en: Experimental Settings
blocks.zh: 实验设置

blocks.en:
Systems. We evaluate four image editing systems that exhibit different levels of safety filtering in practice.
Google’s gemini-2.5-flash-image (Gemini), OpenAI’s gpt-image-1-mini (GPT), and Alibaba’s qwen-image-edit-plus-2025-12-15 (Qwen API) are accessed via commercial APIs and produce allow, refuse, or error responses.
Qwen API is based on the open-source Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (Qwen Local), so that their comparison isolates the contribution of the deployment wrapper.
This provides insight into the safety mechanisms in the Qwen API system regardless of the base Qwen Local model.
All systems use default settings without modification.
This yields 5,940 × 4 = 23,760 5{,}940\times 4=23{,}760 system runs.
blocks.zh:
系统 我们评价了四个图像编辑系统,这些系统在实践中显示不同程度的安全过滤。
Google的Gemini-2.5-flash-image(Gemini),OpenAI的gpt-image-1-mini(GPT),以及Alibaba的qwen-image-edit-plus-2025-12-15(Quen API)通过商业API访问,并制作允许,拒绝,或错误回复.
Quen API基于开源的Quen/Quen-Image-Edit-2511(Quen Local),因此他们的比较隔离了部署包装器的贡献.
这提供了对Quen API系统中的安全机制的洞察,而不论基础的Quen本地模式.
所有系统使用默认设置而无需修改.
此值为 5 940 × 4 = 23. 760 5{,} 940\ times 4=23{,}760系统运行.

blocks.en:
Implementation. All images are preprocessed to 2048px maximum dimension in PNG format.
Samples that returned transient errors were re-run three times after the initial evaluation, eliminating all technical errors for Gemini and GPT.
Qwen API retains some persistent platform-level blocks reporting “Error code: 404”, which we keep as Error since their mechanism is opaque.
Note that all three metrics (SOR, UIR, UNR) are defined over Block = Refuse+Error, so this classification does not affect the reported results.
blocks.zh:
执行。 所有图像都以PNG格式预处理到2048px最大尺寸.
返回瞬态误差的样本在初始评价后重新运行三次,消除了双子座和GBT的所有技术错误.
Quen API保留了一些持续的平台级块,报告“错误代码:404”,我们将其保留为错误,因为它们的机制不透明。
注意所有三个度量衡(SOR,UIR,UNR)都是在Block = Reference+Error上定义的,因此这一分类不影响报告的结果.

blocks.en: Overall Performance
blocks.zh: 总体业绩

blocks.en:
Table 1 summarizes the main results across four systems.
Gemini and GPT actively refuse 41.5–43.9% of requests on unsafe images, while both Qwen variants show near-zero explicit refusal.
Qwen API blocks 6.8% of requests through persistent platform-level errors, suggesting a basic content wrapper.
The three metrics reveal a clear pattern: all systems with any safety filtering achieve high UIR but low UNR, indicating text-driven rather than vision-aware safety.
We analyze this pattern along three dimensions: text-vision interaction (Section 4.3 ), edit intent (Section 4.4 ), and image risk category (Section 4.5 ).
blocks.zh:
表1概述了四个系统的主要成果。
双子座和GPT在不安全图像上积极拒绝41.5–43.9%的请求,而Quen两个变体都显示出近乎零的明确拒绝.
Quen API通过持续的平台级别错误来阻断6.8%的请求,提示了一个基本内容包.
三个度量衡揭示了一个明确的模式:所有具有任何安全过滤功能的系统都实现了高UIR但低UNR,表明文字驱动而非视觉感知安全.
我们从三个方面分析这一模式:文本-视觉互动(第4.3节)、编辑意图(第4.4节)和图像风险类别(第4.5节)。

blocks.en: Text-Vision Safety Mismatch
blocks.zh: 文本视觉安全错配

blocks.en:
As shown in Table 1 , Gemini and GPT achieve high UIR (87.1% and 81.6%), refusing most unsafe-intent edits regardless of whether the input image is safe or unsafe.
However, their UNR is only 24.2% and 22.4%: even when the input image contains violence or hate, these systems allow neutral edits such as “improve the image quality” (Figure 1 ).
Qwen API exhibits a similar pattern at lower magnitude (UIR 7.2%, UNR 12.0%), suggesting it applies basic text-level content filtering.
blocks.zh:
如表1所示,双子座和GPT实现高UIR(87.1%和81.6%),拒绝最不安全的意向编辑,无论输入图像是安全还是不安全.
然而,他们的UNR只有24.2%和22.4%:即使输入的图像包含暴力或仇恨,这些系统允许中立的编辑,如“改善图像质量”(图1)。
Quen API在低级显示类似模式(UIR 7.2%,UNR 12.0%),建议它应用基本的文本级别内容过滤.

blocks.en:
This mismatch also manifests as over-refusal on safe images.
Gemini and GPT show SOR of 14.0% and 11.5%, blocking benign edits on safe images that depict risk-adjacent themes (e.g., a safe image in the “violence” category).
The held-out validation in Section 4.7 further confirms this, e.g., SOR of Gemini drops from 14.0% to 3.6% on topically neutral images.
blocks.zh:
这种不匹配也表现在安全图像上的过度反驳.
双子座和GPT显示的SOR为14.0%和11.5%,在描绘风险相邻主题的安全图像(如“暴力”类别中的安全图像)上屏蔽良性编辑.
第4.7节中被搁置的验证进一步证实了这一点,例如,双子座的SOR在主题中性图像上从14.0%下降到3.6%.

blocks.en: Finding 1: Text-Vision Safety Mismatch Gemini and GPT refuse more unsafe-intent edits (UIR) than unsafe images with neutral instructions (UNR), revealing that safety awareness is primarily text-driven.
blocks.zh: 发现1:Text-Vision Security Missmatch 双子座和GPT拒绝比带有中性指令(UNR)的不安全图像更不安全的意向编辑(UIR),揭示安全意识主要是由文本驱动的.

blocks.en:
Table 2 : Average moderation scores and allow rates (%) by image safety label and edit intent.
The moderation score of “Image only” is the average score for all images, while “+[Edit Intent]” represents the average score of the image-instruction pairs.
The scores are dominated by visual content (Unsafe+Neutral: 0.195 > > Safe+Unsafe-Intent: 0.113), yet the allow rates are driven by text intent (the safe-vs-unsafe gap under unsafe-intent edits is only 0.2–0.4% for Gemini/GPT, while the gap under neutral edits is 13–16%).
blocks.zh:
表2:按图像安全标签和编辑意图分列的平均温和分数和允许率(%)。
“只有图像”的温和分数是所有图像的平均分数,而“+[编辑意 ”代表图像指示对的平均分数。
评分以视觉内容为主(Unsafe+Neutral:0.195 > > Safe+unsafe-Intent:0.113),然而允许率是由文本意向驱动的(在不安全的inteds下的安全vs-unsafe差距对双子座/GPT只有0.2-0.4%,而中性编辑下的缺口为13-16%).

blocks.en:
Figure 5 : Per-prompt allow rates (top) and text-only moderation scores (bottom).
Neutral and risk-reducing prompts yield consistent allow rates ( > > 82%), while unsafe-intent prompts show sharp drops in Gemini/GPT.
blocks.zh:
图5:每时每刻允许比率(最高)和只限文本的节制分数(最低)。
中性和降低风险的导出率一致( > 82%),而不安全的导出率则显示出双子座/GPT的急剧下降。

blocks.en: On Edit Intents
blocks.zh: 编辑意向

blocks.en:
Table 2 jointly presents moderation scores and system allow rates by image safety and edit intent.
Unsafe images with neutral edits show a higher moderation score of 0.195 than safe images with unsafe-intent edits (0.113).
However, system decisions are not consistent with this tendency.
Under unsafe-intent instructions, image safety has near-zero influence: the safe-vs-unsafe gap is only 0.4% for Gemini (13.1% vs 12.7%) and 0.2% for GPT (18.5% vs 18.3%).
Under neutral instructions, the gap widens to 13.6% (Gemini) and 15.7% (GPT), indicating that some visual sensitivity exists but remains far weaker than text-based filtering.
blocks.zh:
表2按图像安全和编辑意图,联合列出适度分数和系统允许分数。
带有中性编辑的不安全图像显示的温和度分数为0.195,高于带有不安全意图编辑的安全图像(0.113)。
然而,系统决定与这一趋势不一致。
在不安全的提示下,图像安全有近乎零的影响:安全Vs-不安全的缺口对双子座来说只有0.4%(13.1%对12.7%),对GPT来说只有0.2%(18.5%对18.3%).
在中性指令下,差距扩大至13.6%(Gemini)和15.7%(GPT),表明存在一些视觉敏感性,但仍远远弱于文本过滤.

blocks.en:
Per-prompt analysis (Figure 5 ) reveals further nuance.
Neutral and risk-reducing prompts yield consistently high allow rates ( > > 82%) across all systems, matching their low moderation scores.
Under unsafe-intent prompts, allow rates drop sharply for Gemini and GPT but not for Qwen.
Notably, GPT refuses 100% of U02 but allows 33% of U01 despite identical text moderation scores (0.063), suggesting keyword-level triggers (e.g., “inappropriate” in U02) rather than semantic understanding.
blocks.zh:
瞬间分析(图5)揭示了进一步的细微差别.
中立和降低风险促使所有系统的产量一直很高( > 82%),与低温得分相匹配。
在不安全的提示下,允许双子座和GPT的速率急剧下降,但不允许Quen.
值得注意的是,GPT拒绝U02的100%,但允许33%的U01,尽管文字温和得分相同(0.063),暗示关键词级触发点(例如U02中的“不恰当”而不是语义理解)。

blocks.en: Finding 2: Text Intent Overrides Visual Risk Although unsafe images with neutral edits have a higher moderation score than safe images with unsafe intent, we observe that text intent dominates system decisions.
blocks.zh: 发现 2: 文本意图覆盖视觉风险 虽然带有中性编辑的不安全图像的温和分数高于带有不安全意图的安全图像,但我们观察到文本意图支配着系统的决定.

blocks.en:
Figure 6 : Per-category allow rates (%) for safe and unsafe images.
Most risk categories have inconsistent awareness among different systems.
Sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity.
blocks.zh:
图6:安全和不安全图像的每个类别允许率(%)。
大多数风险类别不同系统的认识不一致。
性内容表现出最强的视觉敏感性.

blocks.en: On Image Risk Category
blocks.zh: 图像风险类别

blocks.en:
Safety Awareness Across Systems. Figure 6 shows per-category allow rates separately for safe and unsafe images.
This reveals an awareness inconsistency across different systems, which also diverges from their stated content policies (see Appendix B ).
Despite all surveyed platforms prohibiting unsafe sexual images, allow rates range from 14.8% (GPT) to 38.1% (Qwen API).
Additionally, GPT allows 70.4% of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8%.
This inconsistency reflects these systems’ different safety focus.
blocks.zh:
安全意识跨系统。 图6显示安全和不安全图像的每个类别允许率。
这表明不同系统的认识不一致,也偏离了它们宣布的内容政策(见附录B)。
尽管所有被调查的平台都禁止不安全的性图像,但允许的比例从14.8%(GPT)到38.1%(Quen API)不等.
此外,GPT允许70.4%的不安全政治内容,而双子座只允许34.8%.
这种不一致反映了这些系统不同的安全重点。

blocks.en: Finding 3: System Safety Awareness Is Inconsistent The same content receives divergent treatment across systems, indicating safety boundaries are system-dependent rather than grounded in shared standards.
blocks.zh: 调查结果3:系统安全意识不一致 同一内容在不同的系统中得到不同的处理,表明安全界限取决于系统而不是基于共同标准。

blocks.en:
Figure 7 : Two unsafe images with the same neutral instruction.
The sexual image (top) is refused by Gemini/GPT, while the violent image (bottom) is allowed.
blocks.zh:
图7:两个带有相同中性指令的不安全图像.
性形象(上)被双子座/GPT拒绝,而暴力形象(下)则被允许.

blocks.en:
Sexual Category. Note that sexual content shows the strongest visual input sensitivity among all categories: the safe-vs-unsafe gap reaches 40.7% for Gemini (65.2% safe vs 24.4% unsafe) and 45.6% for GPT (60.4% vs 14.8%).
Even Qwen API’s wrapper catches 61.9% of unsafe sexual content via errors, exhibiting a safe-vs-unsafe gap of 57.8%.
By contrast, categories like hate and illegal activity show near-zero or negative gaps, e.g., GPT allows 65.9% of safe hate images vs 68.1% of unsafe ones.
Figure 7 shows a concrete example of two unsafe images with neutral editing instructions.
This exception likely reflects the maturity of NSFW classifiers [ 5 ] , which have been deployed for over a decade [ 4 ] .
Categories like hate speech or political content are inherently more context-dependent and harder to detect from visual features alone.
This sexual content awareness demonstrates that visual-input-aware filtering is technically feasible, while the challenge is extending this capability to the remaining categories.

性分类。 注意性内容在所有类别中表现出最强的视觉输入敏感性:双子座的安全-vs-不安全差距达到40.7%(65.2%的安全对24.4%不安全),GPT达到45.6%(60.4%对14.8%).
连Quen API的包装也通过错误捕获了61.9%的不安全性内容,显示出安全vs-不安全差距为57.8%.

图7显示了两个带有中性编辑指令的不安全图像的具体实例.

仇恨言论或政治内容等类别本身就更依赖背景,更难从视觉特征中发现。
这种对性内容的认识表明,视觉输入-感知过滤在技术上是可行的,而挑战在于将这种能力扩大到其余类别。

blocks.en: Safety-Utility Trade-off
blocks.zh: 安全实用性

blocks.en:
Figure 8 places all four systems in safety-utility space, using SOR as the utility axis (over-refusal of benign edits) and UIR/UNR as safety axes.
The four systems span the full trade-off spectrum: Qwen Local achieves perfect utility (0% SOR) but zero safety; Qwen API adds marginal filtering (7.2% UIR); Gemini and GPT trade utility for safety but still allow over 75% of neutral edits on unsafe images.
No system reaches the ideal upper-left region of either panel, indicating that jointly optimizing text-and-vision-aware safety remains an open challenge.

没有任何系统到达两个小组的理想左上角区域,这表明共同优化文本和视觉安全仍然是一个公开的挑战。

blocks.en: Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 阅读研究

blocks.en:
Image Source. As shown in Figure 9 , we find that systems treat human-crafted and AI-generated images with little difference.
For instance, allow rate differences between sources are under 2% for Gemini, GPT, and Qwen Local, confirming source-agnostic filtering.
Qwen API shows a slightly lower allow rate on AI-generated images, which might indicate an identification difference within its filter.
blocks.zh:
图片来源. 如图9所示,我们发现系统处理人造和人工智能生成的图像,没有什么差别。
例如,允许双子座、GBT和Quen本地源之间的比率差异低于2%,这证实了源不可知过滤。
Quen API在AI生成的图像上显示的允许率略低,这可能表明其过滤器内的识别差异.

blocks.en:
Held-Out Validation. To verify that our findings are not limited to UnsafeBench, we construct a held-out control set of 200 natural images randomly sampled from MagicBrush [ 33 ] , paired with all nine edit prompts (1,800 samples).
As MagicBrush is an instruction-guided real image editing dataset, we consider the collected images as safe and unrelated to specific risk categories.
Then, we compare the held-out dataset with EditSafetyBench ’s safe split ( EditSafetyBench -Safe).
Specifically, we compute SOR and UIR on these safe-only images as R Safe × (Neutral+Risk-Reducing) Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{Safe $\times$ (Neutral+Risk-Reducing)}} and R Safe × Unsafe-Intent Block R^{\text{Block}}_{\text{Safe $\times$ Unsafe-Intent}} .
As the Qwen series exhibits little safety alignment, we only evaluate on Gemini and GPT.
blocks.zh:
Hold-Out 验证。 为了证实我们的发现并不限于Unsafe Bench,我们构建了一套由200个自然图像随机抽样从MagicBrush [33] 中组成的被搁置的控制集,与所有9个编辑提示(1,800个样本)对齐.
由于MagicBrush是一个指导性真实图像编辑数据集,我们认为收集的图像是安全的,与特定的风险类别无关.
然后,我们将被搁置的数据集与EditSafety Bench的安全分割(EditSafety Bench - Safe)进行比较.
具体地说,我们在这些安全图像上计算 SOR 和 UIR 作为 R Safe × (Neutral+ Risk- Reduction) Block RQQText{BlockQText{Safe $\times$(Neutral+Risk-Reduction)}} 和 R Safe × Unsafe-Intent Block RXQText{BlockQText{ $\time$ Unsafe-Intent_} (中文(简体) ).
由于Quen系列显示的安全性不高,我们只评价双子座和GPT.

blocks.en:
Results in Table 3 show that SOR drops substantially on the held-out set (Gemini: 3.6% vs. 14.0%; GPT: 0.7% vs. 11.5%).
This indicates that although images in EditSafetyBench -Safe are safe, they are more prone to trigger refusals as their visual themes overlap with risk categories.
For instance, a safe image in the “violence” category might trigger the refusal.
This confirms that Gemini and GPT do incorporate some degree of visual content awareness into their safety decisions: risk category-related imagery may raise the refusal rate.
For UIR, Gemini remains consistent across datasets (88.8% vs. 87.1%), while GPT shows a notable drop on the held-out set (68.5% vs. 81.6%), suggesting that the visual context of risk-category images in EditSafetyBench makes GPT more cautious toward unsafe-intent edits.

例如,“暴力”类的安全形象可能会触发拒绝。
这证实了双子座和GPT的确在其安全决定中纳入了一定程度的视觉内容意识:与风险类别相关的图像可能会提高拒绝率.
对于UIR,双子座数据组(88.8%对87.1%)依然一致,而GPT显示被搁置的集(68.5%对81.6%)明显下降,这表明EditSafety Bench中风险类图像的视觉背景使得GPT对不安全的内在编辑更加谨慎.

blocks.en: Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论情况

blocks.en:
Why the Text-Vision Gap Exists. Current safety mechanisms likely originate from single-modality pipelines, where the primary threat is a harmful text or image [ 12 , 9 , 14 ] .
Image editing requires considering both text and visual modalities together.
Our findings indicate that Gemini and GPT mainly focus on the text modality, while the Qwen series exhibits little awareness of unsafe editing attempts.
Additionally, our held-out validation (see Section 4.7 ) confirms that some visual awareness exists (risk category-related safe images trigger higher SOR), but it remains far weaker than text-based filtering.
A practical path forward could combine a policy-adaptive image guardrail [ 30 , 20 ] with intent-aware decision logic, allowing risk-reducing edits on unsafe images while blocking harm-amplifying ones.
blocks.zh:
为什么文字-视觉差距是存在的。 目前的安全机制可能源于单一模式管道,主要威胁是有害的文字或图像[12、9、14]。
图像编辑需要同时考虑文本和视觉模式。
我们的研究结果表明,双子座和GPT主要关注文本模式,而Quen系列则很少显示出对不安全编辑尝试的认识.
此外,我们被搁置的验证(见第4.7节)证实,存在一些视觉意识(与风险类别有关的安全图像触发更高的SOR),但它仍然远远弱于文本过滤。
一条切实可行的前进道路可以将一个政策适应性图像护栏[30,20]与意向性决定逻辑相结合,允许在不安全图像上进行减少风险的编辑,同时阻断伤害的复制。

blocks.en:
Unsafe Images × \times Neutral Edit Intent. Our benchmark characterizes system behavior but does not prescribe a single correct answer for all scenarios.
For unsafe images with neutral instructions (e.g., “adjust brightness” on a violent image), the appropriate response is debatable: the instruction is benign, the unsafe content already exists, and the edit may not create new harm.
But refusing will protect against the redistribution of harm, e.g., refusing to amplify the quality of an unsafe sexual/hate image.
The answer depends on the deployment context and platform policy. EditSafetyBench provides the empirical tools to measure where systems currently draw this line and to track how it evolves.
blocks.zh:
不安全的图像 ×\times 中立编辑意图 。 我们的基准是系统行为的特点,但并没有为所有情况规定一个正确的答案。
对于带有中性指令的不安全图像(如暴力图像上的"正当亮度"),适当的反应是有争议的:指令是良性的,不安全的内容已经存在,编辑可能不会造成新的伤害.
但拒绝将防止伤害的再分配,例如拒绝扩大不安全的性/仇恨形象的质量。
答案取决于部署背景和平台政策。 EditSafety Bench提供了经验工具,用来衡量系统目前绘制此线的位置,并跟踪其演化过程.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduce EditSafetyBench , a benchmark for measuring system-level safety awareness in instruction-guided image editing.
By pairing safe and unsafe images with three types of edit intents across 11 risk categories, EditSafetyBench reveals whether deployed systems jointly consider visual content and textual intent in their safety decisions.
Our evaluation of four systems exposes a systematic text-vision safety mismatch.
At the category level, most risk categories exhibit notable cross-platform inconsistency, while sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity.
These findings demonstrate that current safety mechanisms, largely inherited from single modality, are insufficient for the multimodal nature of image editing.
We hope EditSafetyBench serves as both a diagnostic tool for existing image editing systems and a catalyst for developing safety guardrails that reason jointly over both modalities.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们引入了EditSafetty Bench,这是在指导图像编辑中衡量系统层面安全意识的基准。
EditSafety Bench将安全和不安全的图像与涉及11个风险类别的三种类型的编辑意图进行配对,揭示了部署的系统是否在其安全决定中共同考虑视觉内容和文字意图。
我们对四个系统的评估暴露出系统化的文本视觉安全不匹配.
在类别层面,大多数风险类别显示出明显的跨平台不一致,而性内容显示出最强的视觉敏感性.
这些调查结果表明,目前主要从单一模式继承的安全机制不足以满足图像编辑的多式联运性质。
我们希望EditSafety Bench既成为现有图像编辑系统的诊断工具,又成为开发安全护栏的催化剂,这些护栏共同为两种模式提供理由。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Decision vs Outcome. We evaluate system-level decisions (allow/refuse/error), not output image harmfulness or editing quality.
A system that allows an edit may still produce a safe output; conversely, a refused request may have been safe to process.
Future work should evaluate output safety alongside input-based decisions.
blocks.zh:
决定与结果。 我们评价系统层面的决定(允许/拒绝/错误),而不是输出图像有害或编辑质量。
允许编辑的系统仍然可以产生安全的输出;反之,被拒绝的请求可能已经安全处理.
今后的工作应当与基于投入的决定一起评价产出的安全性。

blocks.en:
Prompt Coverage. The 9-prompt bank covers three intent types but cannot exhaustively represent all editing requests.
Adversarial prompt engineering or indirect unsafe requests may reveal different safety boundaries.
blocks.zh:
即时报道 9时制库涵盖三种意向类型,但不能详尽地代表所有编辑请求.
横向即时工程或间接的不安全请求可能揭示出不同的安全界限.

blocks.en:
Image Representativeness. Images are drawn from UnsafeBench across 11 categories with balanced human-crafted and AI-generated sources.
Our held-out validation with MagicBrush confirms that findings generalize beyond UnsafeBench, though neither dataset fully captures the diversity of real user uploads.
blocks.zh:
影像代表性. 图片取材自Unsafe Bench,分为11个类别,拥有均衡的人造和AI生成的来源.
我们与MagicBrush的搁置验证证实,发现的泛泛于Unsafe Bench之外,尽管两个数据集都完全抓住了真实用户上传的多样性.

blocks.en:
Temporal Validity. Commercial systems may update their safety filters after our evaluation period.
Thus, we use stable versions and provide a detailed description in Appendix E . EditSafetyBench is designed for repeated evaluation as systems evolve.

暂时有效。 商业系统可以在评估期过后更新其安全过滤器。
因此,我们使用稳定的版本,并在附录E中提供详细的描述。 随着系统的发展,Edit Safety Bench是为重复评价而设计的.

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
EditSafetyBench provides a reusable framework for tracking progress in text-vision safety as image editing systems continue to evolve.
Our work builds on existing datasets and publicly accessible image editing systems, which are used solely for this research.
We are committed to sharing our artifacts with the research community for research purposes, including the dataset, analysis scripts, and configuration information.
The released artifacts will clearly state that they are intended for research purposes only and that any misuse is strictly prohibited.
We also disclose our use of AI assistance in Appendix A .

我们的工作以现有数据集和可公开查阅的图像编辑系统为基础,这些系统仅用于这项研究。
